title: Forgeworks strategic inference check-in
summary: Quarterly check-in to review Forgeworks' inference usage, rising costs, reliability incidents in Feb, and roadmap alignment for Q2. Discussed Dedicated vs Hosted capacity, VPC/private deployment constraints, encryption/KMS requirements, and a pilot stress test. Agreed on next steps: Redwood to share updated pricing and pilot terms, Forgeworks to provide a short test prompt set and schedule a benchmark window.
next_steps: Maya: send updated pricing + pilot term sheet (target 2026-03-06)
Forgeworks (Aisha/Carlos): share 50 prompt test set and expected QPS profile (by 2026-03-05)
Liam: schedule 3-hour dedicated pool stress benchmark and share test steps (by 2026-03-10)
Priya: set up recurring weekly check-ins during pilot
action_items: Maya: share updated pricing & pilot term sheet by 2026-03-06
Liam: run 3-hour stress benchmark on dedicated pool (2.2B model) and send results by 2026-03-10
Aisha: provide 50 prompt golden set and throughput expectations by 2026-03-05
Ben: confirm network egress/cidr and firewall for VPC peering by 2026-03-08
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-03
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 62 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Priya (CSM), Aisha (Forgeworks), Carlos (Forgeworks), Sophie (Forgeworks), Ben (Forgeworks)

Summary (auto): Quick QBR-style check-in focused on costs and uptime; agreed to pilot a dedicated pool and run benchmarks; security items (KMS/SOC2) noted for legal follow-up.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood): hey everyone, thanks for making time, appreciate it. agenda for today: usage/cost review, reliability incidents from feb, then we want to talk about options—dedicated vs hosted vs private—and wrap with pilot next steps. does that align with what you were expecting?
[00:18] Aisha (Forgeworks): yeah that sounds right, uh we're mostly worried about the spike in token spend last month and a couple of 5-10s latency blips that caused retries in our ingestion pipeline.
[00:30] Carlos: and just to add, we saw a couple of errors when the KV cache warmed up after the deploy, so throughput dipped. not a full outage but enough to trigger pagerduty.
[00:44] Liam (Redwood SE): okay, thanks for that. quick housekeeping: for the latency blips we pulled traces and they show a couple of backend queue buildups during peak QPS—likely batching parameter spikes and occasional model fallback to a larger variant. i can share the trace links after.
[01:05] Sophie (Forgeworks): were those fallbacks within the same model family? because our cost jumped when requests landed on the larger model.
[01:12] Liam: yeah, looks like a fallback path routed to a 13B variant; routing policy defaulted because of capacity congestion. we can tune routing to prefer cheaper compatible variants and enable earlier KV caching to avoid re-compute.
[01:30] Aisha: is that a hosted-only behavior? we were thinking dedicated would avoid those fallbacks.
[01:36] Maya: good question. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and reduces routing to other model sizes in hosted fleet, but it's not a magic bullet—if you pick the smallish pool and then go above expected QPS you can still see contention unless you configure burst capacity.
[01:50] Ben (Forgeworks): can we get a concrete cost delta? we run about 1.2M tokens / day on average and had spikes to 2.6M.
[01:59] Maya: internally we estimate unit economics per 1M tokens with your current model profile: hosted baseline is $X (placeholder) per million; with fallback to larger models during spikes you saw a 40-60% effective cost increase. Dedicated reserved capacity gives us a flatter effective cost at committed throughput; we'll send a tailored price table.
[02:20] Carlos: and what about prefix/KV caching? we think a lot of our prompts are repeated and could be cached more aggressively.
[02:28] Liam: absolutely—prefix caching and continuous KV caching can shave off token compute for repeated contexts. right now i think your cache hit rate is low—about 18% from the telemetry we sampled. target for you could be 45-60% with prompt engineering and shorter keying.
[02:45] Sophie: quick question on the private deployment option—we have to meet internal compliance: SSO via SAML, KMS with our HSM, audit logs forwarded to a central SIEM. how mature is Redwood Private on those integrations?
[02:58] Maya: Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS/HSM integrations and audit log forwarding. SAML SSO, RBAC and centralized logging are available. i will attach the security pack and a SOC 2 snapshot. legal may want more, but we do have on-prem patterns.
[03:15] Aisha: do we need to wait for private? or can we start with dedicated hosted then migrate to private later?
[03:21] Priya (CSM): many customers start hosted -> dedicated -> private; migrating is supported, but we recommend pinning model versions and validating rollback/traceability before doing the switch. migration windows can be scheduled.
[03:35] Ben: any network work for VPC peering in private mode? our infra team needs to know expected ports and CIDR ranges.
[03:41] Liam: for VPC peering we provide an ingress policy doc; most customers open specific egress ports + we coordinate the peer. i'll attach a checklist.
[03:52] Maya: okay, let's move to the feb incidents quick postmortem—Carlos can you summarize?
[03:58] Carlos: sure. feb 17th around 22:10 UTC we saw elevated token latency for about 12 minutes. root cause: a model rollout induced kernel selection change on the serving runtime, causing some nodes to thrash while the kernel cache rebuilt. there was an automated fallback but it created a heavier model route for ~3 minutes due to a race in the routing config.
[04:26] Liam: hm that kernel selection thrash—i mentioned that to infra, we actually pushed a mitigation last week that looks to be stable. the race in routing config is something we can guard with stricter rollout windows; we can also pin a canary ratio lower.
[04:42] Aisha: is there an SLA hit here? we had a customer-visible slowdown and we need a write-up for our execs.
[04:48] Maya: we'll produce an incident summary with timeline and mitigations; Priya will own the write-up and we'll add it to the portal.
[04:56] Priya: noted. i'll draft and share by 2026-03-05.
[05:03] Sophie: back to economics—if we reserve dedicated capacity how flexible is autoscaling and burst? we expect marketing-driven surges occasionally.
[05:12] Maya: Dedicated supports configurable autoscale policies and burst capacity. you can define baseline reserved throughput and set a burst budget (minutes of extra QPS) that we honor when capacity available. we can show historical surge fits into a burst plan.
[05:25] Aisha: what about model quantization—could we drop to an 8-bit variant and save cost without degrading UX?
[05:31] Liam: yes, quantization + mixed precision can yield 2-3x throughput gains for some architectures. the tradeoff is occasional quality deltas; we recommend running an eval suite on your golden prompts to measure fidelity. Redwood Optimize can automate quantization recommendations per workload.
[05:50] Carlos: do you support server-side evals? we'd prefer Redwood to run the batch evals against proposed quantized weights.
[05:57] Maya: yes, we can run a quality regression suite as an add-on and provide metrics and mismatch examples. we'll scope that if you want.
[06:06] Aisha: yes, let's include that in pilot scope.
[06:10] Maya: great. next, plan for the pilot/benchmark: here's a proposed approach—provide 50-100 representative prompts, define expected QPS, Redwood will provision a dedicated pool with your model of choice (we can host a quantized variant), run a 3-hour stress window including ramp and soak, and produce latency, p50/p95/p99, and cost per token metrics with caching on/off.
[06:36] Ben: what's the model we should pick for this? current prod is a 2.2B family; we also evaluate a 7B variant for some heavier flows.
[06:44] Liam: start with your 2.2B poly model in the config. we'll do a second run with the 7B and ideally a quantized 2.2B to show tradeoffs.
[06:54] Sophie: for our legal folks—can Redwood provide a data handling note? specifically retention, logs, and deletes for prompt/response pairs?
[07:02] Maya: yes, data retention policies and a DSAR playbook are available—i'll include it. for the pilot we can enable prompt redaction and TTL-based deletion.
[07:13] Aisha: earlier you mentioned KV cache hit rate improvements—what are the recommended changes on our side?
[07:19] Liam: two items: revise prompt keying to reduce variance (so fewer unique cache keys), and add a short client-side prefix index so that repeated preambles don't create new cache entries. we can share a snippet and a before/after sim.
[07:34] Carlos: ok we'll try that.
[07:36] [08:00] Maya: small aside—billing anomalies: we noticed some billing tags were missing from a set of test routes which made attribution noisy. Ben, can your team ensure your route metadata is set for the test IDs?
[08:12] Ben: yes, we'll patch that tonight.
[08:17] [08:30] Aisha: i want to set success criteria for the pilot: 1) p95 latency under 450ms for the 2.2B model, 2) cost per 1M tokens reduced by at least 30% vs the feb baseline, 3) KV cache hit rate over 45%. are those reasonable?
[08:45] Liam: reasonable and measurable. we'll aim to instrument logs and share a dashboard.
[08:50] Maya: circling back to compliance: Sophie, you mentioned SSO/SAML and KMS—do you need an architecture diagram?
[08:56] Sophie: yes we need a diagram for our infra review and a list of supported KMS providers.
[09:02] Maya: i'll include diagrams and a supported KMS matrix.
[09:06] [09:30] Carlos: any blockers from Redwood's side to start the pilot in the next week?
[09:35] Maya: no major blockers. we'll need your prompt set and QPS profile and a signed pilot terms sheet. i can send the pilot term sheet template right after this call.
[09:45] Priya: we'll also set up weekly status syncs during the pilot and a dedicated slack channel for logs and quick triage.
[09:54] Aisha: good. a question: do you log inference inputs by default for debugging? we have tight privacy rules.
[09:59] Liam: by default we log telemetry but input logging can be disabled. for debugging we typically use redacted examples; we can also provide a redaction SDK.
[10:11] Sophie: ok thanks.
[10:13] [10:30] Maya: a couple of commercial notes: because you expect surges, we can propose a hybrid pricing: committed reserved throughput plus an elastic spot buffer that bills at a slightly higher rate. that helps you avoid surprising bills during bursts.
[10:45] Ben: sounds workable—we just need predictability for finance.
[10:49] Maya: we'll include a projection sheet with three scenarios: baseline, marketing surge, and retail-promo peak.
[10:57] [11:20] Aisha: any concerns about deprecation windows or model rollouts that could affect us? we want advance notice.
[11:27] Liam: we have a model lifecycle policy and try to give 30-60 day notice for major rollouts. for dedicated customers you can pin a model version for longer.
[11:36] Sophie: great. last question—are there specific infra knobs we should be aware of to reduce p99?
[11:43] Liam: yes—batch size caps, prefetching, kv cache warmers, and having a soft-priority queue for low-latency routes. we can share recommended config tuned to your QPS distribution.
[11:54] Maya: ok wrapping up, let's recap actions and owners.
[11:58] Priya: recap - Redwood: pilot term sheet, security pack, diagrams, pricing scenarios, schedule benchmark. Forgeworks: prompt set, QPS profile, CIDR and firewall info. run dates: aim for week of 2026-03-08.
[12:15] Aisha: that works, thanks.
[12:17] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll follow up with the artifacts. end of call.

Notes on transcript quality: some speaker labels were auto-attributed; a few product names and acronyms may be slightly mis-transcribed (e.g., "KV cash" vs KV cache, "Redwood Dedi" vs Redwood Dedicated).

References / links mentioned (will share via follow-up): pilot term sheet template, security pack (SOC2 snapshot & KMS matrix), kernel-selection mitigation changelog, trace links for feb 17 incident, billing tag checklist, benchmark runbook.

End of transcript.
